# Incremental Ticket Export (Cursor-based)

## Prerequisites

- Must be an Admin (Allowed for: **Admins**)
- Your Zendesk instance must support the Incremental Exports API

## Method

`GET`

## URL

`https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor`

## Description

Returns tickets that changed since a specified start time using Zendesk’s **cursor-based incremental export** mechanism. Cursor-based exports are recommended because they provide more consistent performance and response sizes than time-based pagination.

## Enforcement Rules

- The request **must** be sent to `/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor`.
- On the **initial** export request, the `start_time` query parameter **must** be provided.
- `start_time` **must be at least one minute in the past**. Data isn’t provided for the most recent minute.
- On **subsequent** requests, use the `cursor` query parameter (from the prior response) and `start_time` is **not required**.
- When executing the action, ensure to send **Query Parameters in the URL** as query parameters, **not** in the body.
- This endpoint has **no request body**.

### Valid Examples

```http
GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?start_time=1332034771
GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?cursor=abc123
GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?cursor=abc123&support_type_scope=agent
```

### Invalid Examples

```http
GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor
# (invalid for the initial request because start_time is missing)

GET /api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?start_time=NOW
# (start_time must be an integer unix timestamp and at least one minute in the past)
```

## Headers

```json
{
  "Accept": "application/json"
}
```

## Required Path Parameters

None

## Required Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---:|---|
| `start_time` | integer | **Required on the initial export request.** Unix timestamp (seconds). Must be at least one minute in the past. Example: `1332034771`. Not required on subsequent cursor-based pagination requests. |

## Optional Query Parameters

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `cursor` | string | Cursor pointer used for subsequent exports after the initial request. |
| `support_type_scope` | string | Lists tickets by support type. Possible values: `"all"`, `"agent"`, `"ai_agent"`. Default: `"agent"`. |

## Response

### Success Response (200 OK)

```json
{
  "after_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMCwiZW5kX3RpbWUiOjE3MTAwMDAwMDB9",
  "after_url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMCwiZW5kX3RpbWUiOjE3MTAwMDAwMDB9",
  "before_cursor": "eyJvZmZzZXQiOjAsImVuZF90aW1lIjoxNzEwMDAwMDAwfQ",
  "before_url": "https://example.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjAsImVuZF90aW1lIjoxNzEwMDAwMDAwfQ",

  "tickets": [
    {
      "id": 12345,
      "subject": "Printer is on fire",
      "description": "Read-only first comment on the ticket.",

      "brand_id": 123,
```

> Note: The scraped documentation lists many possible `tickets[]` fields; the response example above is representative and uses only fields explicitly described.

### Error Responses

Not provided in the scraped content.

## Response Fields

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `after_cursor` | string | Cursor to retrieve the next page of results. |
| `after_url` | string | Full URL to retrieve the next page (contains `cursor`). |
| `before_cursor` | string | Cursor to retrieve the previous page of results (if supported/available). |
| `before_url` | string | Full URL to retrieve the previous page (contains `cursor`). |
| `end_of_stream` | boolean | Whether there are no more results to return. |
| `tickets` | array | Array of ticket objects that changed since the export start time. |

### Ticket object (selected fields from scraped content)

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `tickets[].id` | integer | Automatically assigned when the ticket is created. |
| `tickets[].subject` | string | Subject value for the ticket. |
| `tickets[].description` | string | Read-only first comment on the ticket. |
| `tickets[].status` | string | Possible values: `new`, `open`, `pending`, `hold`, `solved`, `closed`. If custom ticket statuses are activated, this is the status category. |
| `tickets[].priority` | string | Possible values: `urgent`, `high`, `normal`, `low`. |
| `tickets[].requester_id` | integer | The user who requested this ticket. *(Marked required in the scraped field list.)* |
| `tickets[].assignee_id` | integer | Agent currently assigned to the ticket. |
| `tickets[].group_id` | integer | Group the ticket is assigned to. |
| `tickets[].brand_id` | integer | Brand id associated with the ticket. |
| `tickets[].created_at` | string | When this record was created. |
| `tickets[].updated_at` | string | When this record last got updated (only if update generates a ticket event). |
| `tickets[].generated_timestamp` | integer | Unix timestamp representing the most accurate reading of when the record was last updated. |
| `tickets[].tags` | array | Array of tags applied to the ticket. |
| `tickets[].custom_fields` | array | Custom fields for the ticket (`id`, `value`). |
| `tickets[].via.channel` | string | How the ticket/event was created (e.g., `web`, `mobile`, `rule`, `system`). |
| `tickets[].via.source` | object | Source details (free-form object). |
| `tickets[].url` | string | API URL of this ticket. |

## Notes

- **Sideloading is supported** for this endpoint, but for performance reasons, `last_audits` sideloads **aren’t supported**.
- Cursor-based incremental exports are “highly encouraged” by Zendesk for consistency in performance and response sizes.

## Sample Request

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?start_time=1332034771' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Example Usage

### Example 1: Initial export (start time)

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?start_time=1332034771' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example 2: Next page using `after_cursor`

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?cursor=eyJvZmZzZXQiOjEwMCwiZW5kX3RpbWUiOjE3MTAwMDAwMDB9' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json'
```

### Example 3: Filter by support type scope

```bash
curl --request GET \
  --url 'https://{{OAUTH_REQUEST_PAYLOAD.formData.ZENDESK_SUBDOMAIN}}.zendesk.com/api/v2/incremental/tickets/cursor?start_time=1332034771&support_type_scope=all' \
  --header 'Accept: application/json'
```

## Behavior

1. **Initial request**: Provide `start_time` to begin the export window.
2. **Server returns**: A page of `tickets` plus cursor links (`after_cursor`, `after_url`, etc.).
3. **Pagination**: Continue by calling the endpoint again with the returned `cursor` value until `end_of_stream` is `true`.

## Gotchas

- If you set `start_time` too recent (within the last minute), you won’t receive data for the most recent minute.
- Don’t try to sideload `last_audits`, it’s explicitly not supported for performance reasons.
